technical_and_design_decisions: U1: Add a new enum value 'UNDEPLOYED' to the existing Mesos SPI status enum to represent the undeployed status, replacing the current 'UNKNOWN' mapping.
U2: Implement a new REST API endpoint (e.g., POST /rabbit/clean) that invokes the existing RabbitBindingCleaner, using Spring MVC and a service layer.
U3: Optimize YARN deployer by parallelizing the deployment of streams and modules using Java concurrency (e.g., ExecutorService) and reducing synchronous I/O bottlenecks.

U4: Upgrade SHDP dependency from current version to 2.2.1 GA, updating Maven/Gradle build files and verifying compatibility with existing Hive and Hadoop versions; prefer backported improvements to avoid breaking changes.
U5: Upgrade Spring Integration dependency to version 4.2.2.GA, updating build files and ensuring no API incompatibilities with current usage.
U6: Modify Kafka bus producer to allow setting a partition key even when there is only one downstream module, by extending the binding configuration to include a default partitioning key expression.
U7: Upgrade Spring Boot and Spring Cloud Build versions to the latest stable releases, updating parent POM or build configuration and resolving any dependency conflicts.
U8: Document the limitations of HSQL DB when used with composed jobs in the project's user guide, including known issues and workarounds.
assumptions: The developer is familiar with the existing codebase, Spring Framework, and the relevant component architectures (Mesos SPI, Rabbit binder, YARN deployer, Kafka bus, etc.).
The project uses Maven or Gradle for build management; CI/CD pipeline is already set up and can run tests automatically.
Each user story can be implemented independently without introducing merge conflicts; integration testing will be performed after all stories are completed.
Effort estimates include analysis, implementation, unit testing, and basic integration testing for each story.
No additional unplanned refactoring or major architectural changes are required beyond the scope of the stories.
The developer has access to required documentation and can reproduce reported issues locally.
The existing test suite provides adequate coverage and will be extended where necessary.
